evidence.sourceExcerpt: Maps Mania Skip to main content Posts Featured November 15, 2026 An Inverted Earth You Can Explore In honor of the #30DayMapChallenge's Inverted theme, Tripgeo has released Atlantis - the Inverted Earth . I've seen a few maps that swap the Earth's land and oceans around, turning familiar continents into vast underwater worlds and ocean basins into towering mountain ranges. But this is the first I've encountered that lets you actually explore the resulting world from the cockpit of your own submarine. In Atlantis: The World Turned Over , the oceans have drained onto the continents, leaving the former seabed exposed as enormous mountain ranges. Meanwhile, every city on Earth has been submerged beneath the newly formed oceans. Your vehicle for exploring this topsy-turvy planet is the Nereid, a fully navigable submarine that you can pilot directly in your browser. You can dive through the drowned streets of familiar cities, explore submerged urban landscapes and venture into the newly flooded continental interiors. Do you need the time and resources to complete it? Apply for the Spencer Fellowship for Education Reporting 2027 . The Spencer Fellowship for Education Reporting is open to journalists and educators who want to develop and publish an ambitious long-form journalism project that advances public understanding of education. Four fellows will be selected for this yearlong program based at Columbia Journalism School. The fellowship combines study and research with advising from faculty experts at Columbia, Teachers College and elsewhere. Financial Support Each residential fellow receives an $85,000 scholarship for personal living expenses. The scholarship is dispensed in four quarters over the course of the academic year. In addition, each fellow receives $7,500 for the year in project expenses, also dispensed in two halves. Separately, the Spencer grant covers the cost of tuition and other student fees, plus basic student health insurance for residential fellows. Non-residential fellows receive a $43,000 stipend and $7,500 project related expenses, dispensed in quarters. Health insurance is not available. Eligibility All U.S. citizens and green card holders are eligible, including working journalists, freelancers and education professionals. There is no academic prerequisite. A college degree is not required. The most successful candidates are those with experience in the field of education journalism, defined in broad terms to include a wide swath of disciplines related to education such as juvenile justice, economics, arts and culture, poverty and the science of learning. Judges look for a demonstrated ability to research and tell stories in a journalistic style. The strength of the project idea is key, along with the candidate’s potential to complete and publish or produce for a general audience. Application Required application materials include: A resume or CV with your professional and educational qualifications. A short narrative autobiography highlighting the personal and professional origins of your commitments to education and journalism. Up to four work samples that demonstrate your approach to using high-quality research to tell compelling education stories for general audiences (stories on related social issues will also be accepted). Work samples may include book excerpts, newspaper and magazine clips, radio and television broadcasts, podcast episodes, film and video excerpts, academic reports and journal articles, and other formats. A proposal essay describing the project you hope to pursue with a Spencer Fellowship. Judges look for ambitious, high-impact projects that draw on high-quality research and make use of narrative journalism techniques such as extensive interviewing and immersive reporting to explore timely, relevant, and under-explored topics in education.
